title: tools/verify_schema_baseline.py --auto-fix references renamed migration GBL-105 (now GBL-133), auto-fix always fails and loops
registered_by: WF03-gh454-20260806 (ISS-0144 fix verification, C4 self-review step)
symptom: `python tools/verify_schema_baseline.py --check-tenants --auto-fix`, when C4-style drift (orphaned public.tenant rows with storage_mode='SCHEMA' and no matching Postgres schema) is detected, attempts to re-apply migrations/GBL-105_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql -- a file that no longer exists at that name (renamed to GBL-133_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql). Auto-fix reports 'ERROR: ... GBL-105_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql not found; cannot auto-fix', then loops (observed printing the same failing re-check + retry block 5 times in a single invocation) until Postgres connections were briefly exhausted (FATAL: sorry, too many clients already) during manual reproduction while verifying GH #454 / ISS-0144's C4 fix.
root_cause_analysis: tools/verify_schema_baseline.py lines 18, 155-156, 166, 168, 186, 260 all hardcode the literal filename GBL-105_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql. The actual current file on disk is migrations/GBL-133_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql -- same anti-pattern class as ISS-0088/GH#337 (stale filename reference surviving a rename), just in a tool script rather than test cleanup code. Not yet determined whether GBL-133 is a straight rename of GBL-105's content or a different/superseding migration; needs verification before blindly updating the literal.
acceptance_criteria: Update tools/verify_schema_baseline.py's hardcoded filename to the current GBL-133_iss0112_schema_ledger_reconcile.sql (after confirming it is the correct successor to GBL-105), or resolve it dynamically by content/purpose rather than a literal filename, to survive future renames.
Add a retry cap / backoff to the auto-fix loop so a genuinely unfixable condition fails fast with a clear error instead of looping and risking connection exhaustion.
Verify --auto-fix actually reconciles a deliberately-orphaned tenant row in a test run.
evidence_file: N/A -- reproduced directly via `python tools/verify_schema_baseline.py --check-tenants --auto-fix` against db_test during WF03-gh454-20260806; the 2 orphaned rows in that run were cleaned up directly via SQL (DELETE FROM public.tenant WHERE id IN (...)) since the tool's own auto-fix path is broken.
